decisive_items: He had a 6-month duration of cough associated with occasional blood streaks
Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy of mediastinal lymph nodes: ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma with mucinous features
A 56-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of polyarthralgia
response.rationale: The patient's symptoms of polyarthralgia and swelling are likely related to the underlying lung cancer, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.

rejected.why: While the patient has been found to have small foci suspicious for metastatic disease, this is not the primary diagnosis.
The negative rheumatoid factor and lack of erosions on radiographs make rheumatoid arthritis less likely.
Lung adenocarcinoma is a component of the paraneoplastic syndrome, but not the primary diagnosis.
